question: Does the project's working flip-length range (3-8) actually require encoded state (Experiment 1), and does higher-temperature generation-only sampling -- no training -- ever produce a non-literal token attempt (Experiment 2)?

experiment_1_load_bearing_regime.n_capped_by_combinatorics_note: lengths 2/3/4 capped below 40 by the actual scenario-space size (8/16/32 distinct starting-state+operations combinations) -- see the unique_sampling.py bug this triggered
experiment_1_load_bearing_regime.conclusion: The project's 3-8 working range sits INSIDE the load-bearing regime. Answer-only accuracy stays near chance (44-55%) throughout 3-8; normal CoT gives a real accuracy boost at nearly every length (up to +30pp at length 6); corrupted-prefill changes the final answer 47.5-75% of the time throughout (length 8 is the softest point at 47.5%, still real). Rules out a non-load-bearing regime as the explanation for zero invention elsewhere in this project.

experiment_2_generation_exploration_audi.consistent_nonliteral_unreviewed_reason: 7 from checkpoint500 T=1.5 exceeded this run's 10-example-per-setting save cap; cap removed in 09_direct_indomain_synthetic_bridge

decoding_noise.description: near-miss spelling or stuck repetition of the literal word

word_echo.description: domain/instruction vocabulary repeated as a stuck pseudo-state

progressive_drift.description: token mutates further each step, anagram-like
progressive_drift.note: plausibly the same instability 04_stability_investigation identified as checkpoint 500's root cause

deliberate_verbalized_attempt.description: model explicitly stated intent to invent a substitute before doing so
deliberate_verbalized_attempt.note: only cases anywhere in this project where invention-seeking was articulated rather than accidental; both single-step, both trivial

experiment_2_generation_exploration_audi.conclusion: checkpoint500's partial_nonliteral rate is 2-6x base/task_only's at matching temperatures -- RL training increased exploration volume without improving quality. No instance anywhere uses different tokens for different true states in a way that tracks actual alternating ground truth. Rules out temperature/sampling as the missing ingredient.

conclusion: Neither a non-load-bearing task regime nor insufficient sampling temperature explains this project's zero-invention finding. The 3-8 length range genuinely requires state tracking (Experiment 1), and no amount of temperature up to 1.5 across 24,000 generations produces genuine state-correlated non-literal encoding on base, task-only, or checkpoint-500 policies (Experiment 2) -- only decoding noise, word-echo, and (checkpoint500-specific) progressive character drift.
next_step: 09_direct_indomain_synthetic_bridge: test a lever that acts before the attempt (demonstrated valid encoded trajectories via an auxiliary loss) rather than after it (reward shaping, 07) or around it (sampling temperature, this stage).
